$comment: GENERATED by `npm run gen:risk` from src/lib/riskFlagCatalog.ts. The handbook at docs/methodology/procurement-risk-flags.md is generated from the same source. MIT licensed; see LICENSE. Flags are pattern signals for review, NOT findings of wrongdoing.

framing.ocp: A fired flag means the behaviour may be a) not at all illicit or suboptimal; b) not illicit, but suboptimal in terms of value for money; or c) illicit.
framing.publisher: We are a public publisher, not a monitoring institution with a legal mandate. Flags fire for review; they are not findings of wrongdoing.
framing.denominator: The CRI's denominator is the checks we could AVAILABLY evaluate, never all checks — a data-poor contract is excluded from a check, never scored 0 on it.

contractIndex.note: Unweighted by design. `legacyWeight` below feeds an internal sort key that nothing renders.

bitOrderNote: APPEND-ONLY. Renumbering re-maps every historic mask; it is a major version change and requires a full cache rebuild.

contractFlags.availability: Always — the register is corpus-wide, so absence means not listed.
Always — company_politicians covers the whole corpus.
Always — the non-MP official link set covers the whole corpus.

threshold.basis: Pair share of the buyer's LIFETIME spend, and only for buyers above the minimum total below (033).

contractFlags.citation: House threshold. 30% of a buyer's spend going to one supplier is the conventional red-flag bar in CEE procurement oversight (Transparency International methodology); the €100,000 floor beneath it is ours.
contractFlags.availability: Computed corpus-wide per (buyer, supplier) pair — but ONLY for buyers whose lifetime spend clears €100,000. Below that a 100% share is arithmetic rather than concentration, so those pairs are excluded from the flag entirely.
Always — the row's own tag decides it.

threshold.basis: ЗОП чл.116 ал.2 — a 50% cap on the CUMULATIVE value of modifications, stricter than the EU per-modification rule. The ал.3 inflation indexation carries its own separate 50% that does NOT count against ал.2, and чл.116 ал.6 exempts sectoral buyers, so the flag detects the cumulative Δ without being able to say which ground it hit.

contractFlags.availability: Only where an annex actually moved the value — an un-amended contract is excluded from the denominator rather than scored 0.

threshold.basis: Months between the company's founding date and the award. Availability is decided per CONTRACTOR, so a bound on the founding-date source moves the DENOMINATOR, not just the numerator — that asymmetry is what made 30.2% of the corpus disagree across the TS/SQL sides before the parity harness existed.

contractFlags.citation: House threshold. A company barely older than the contract it won is a structural signal, not a rule from a named index — an earlier draft of this catalogue cited a 'K-Index P4' that does not exist.
contractFlags.availability: Only where the contractor's founding date is known and precedes the award.

contractFlags.citation: ЗОП чл.20 ал.4 / чл.21. Reference implementations: OCP R049, ProZorro RISK-2-5/2-6, K-Index P3.
contractFlags.availability: Always — but it is a QUESTION, not a verdict: чл.21 permits separate recurring needs, and the data cannot distinguish that from splitting.
Always server-side — the appeal corpus is joined corpus-wide.

threshold.basis: STRUCTURAL SUPPRESSION, at 2-digit CPV DIVISION grain: where a division's own single-bid share reaches this, one bid is the market's norm rather than a signal. The flag's second, GRADED arm keys on the 5-digit CPV PREFIX median instead (competitive markets only, median ≥ 3) — two different grains in one flag, which is the detail most often restated wrongly.

contractFlags.citation: EC Single Market Scoreboard; ЗОП чл.79 ал.1 т.3
contractFlags.availability: Only where the realised bid count is known.

contractFlags.citation: EC Single Market Scoreboard ("no calls for bids")
contractFlags.availability: Only where a procedure type or a no-notice rationale is recorded.

threshold.basis: Lifted from EU Directive 2014/24 Art. 27 as a round reference figure. ⚠️ That makes it a LEGAL MINIMUM rather than a calibrated risk threshold — Art. 27's own minima are longer and tiered (35 days, 30 with electronic submission, 15 under an accelerated procedure), so 14 is our simplification of it and not a rule the Directive states. The project's own methodology (risk-v2 §6a) records the cut as uncalibrated and due to be re-cut into bands. The TENDER-grain rushedDeadline deliberately differs (12 days, competitive tiers only), because on low-value tiers a short window is statutory rather than anomalous.

contractFlags.citation: EU Dir 2014/24 Art. 27 (a reference figure, not a rule it states)
contractFlags.availability: Only where both tender-window dates are present and ordered.
contractFlags.caveat: CURRENTLY INERT. The tender-window columns are unpopulated across the contracts corpus, so this check is evaluable on effectively no contracts — measured 0 of 20,000 sampled. It is neither firing nor passing: it is excluded from every contract's CRI denominator. Listed here because it is implemented and would begin scoring the moment those dates arrive, not because it contributes today.

contractFlags.availability: Only where the contractor's declared НКИД division is known AND the contract carries a CPV.

tenderFlags.citation: EC Single Market Scoreboard ("no calls for bids")
tenderFlags.availability: Only where a procedure type is recorded.

threshold.basis: TIER-CONDITIONAL, and deliberately NOT the 14-day EU legal minimum. Scored only on the competitive tiers (Открита процедура / Публично състезание), where medians are 30d and 21d; on low-value tiers a ~10-day window is statutory, and 44% of 'Събиране на оферти' sits at 7–11 days.

tenderFlags.availability: Competitive tiers only, with both dates present.

threshold.basis: Award decided within this many days of the submission deadline, INCLUSIVE — the implementation compares `<= 4`, so a 4-day decision fires. (An earlier draft of this catalogue published it as `< 4`, which is off by one day.)

tenderFlags.availability: Only once the procedure is awarded.
tenderFlags.caveat: DIRECTION UNSETTLED. The flag scores SHORT decision periods, but PRWP 10444's own prose justifies risk via the opposite mechanism — that a lengthy decision period gives room for repeated legal challenges until the award reaches a chosen company. The calibration penalises short while the source narrative worries about long: an inconsistency in the source, documented rather than resolved. Treat this as the weakest of the four tender checks.

threshold.basis: Awards summing above this multiple of the procedure estimate. ONE-SIDED by design: awards UNDER the estimate are usually competition savings, and OCP R016's under-valuation is a different comparison (estimate vs the peer-CPV norm), which the normalcy panel already carries. The 10% buffer absorbs rounding and minor scope changes — median awarded/estimated is 99%, p95 is 105%.

tenderFlags.citation: PwC/Ecorys (2013), the only source with measured per-flag weights. ⚠️ Those weights are conditional on a 50/50 case-control sample, so they order flags rather than estimate precision — and an earlier draft of this catalogue cited a specific flag number from it that could not be verified in-repo.
tenderFlags.availability: Only where a procedure estimate and at least one award exist.

exposureGrades.note: TWO weight sets. Availability-weighted mean; an unavailable component is dropped from the denominator, never scored 0.
exposureGrades.supplierOpenQuestion: The supplier arm carries the pre-2026-07-18 direct/singleBid weights and has no upheld-appeal component. Whether that is a deliberate exception or unreviewed drift is undecided; both sets are published as facts.

neutralDisclosures.availability: Where the contractor is, or is linked to, a foreign-funded NGO.
neutralDisclosures.note: Neutral disclosure. Never affects the CRI or any grade.
